title: Microclass provenance + fallback rules (scratchbook)
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad to collect rules & examples for microclass labeling and how to store provenance so downstream ops and model-evals can reason about label source and reliability. NOT final. Mix of heuristics, mini-experiments, and open questions.

Background/context:
- We are increasing use of fine-grained (micro) labels for user-facing features (e.g., intent-subtype, entity-variant). These are useful for product telemetry but often have low inter-annotator agreement.
- Need a lightweight provenance schema so we can: (1) filter training vs eval sets by label origin (human/adjudicated/heuristic/auto-suggest), (2) weight labels during model training or active learning, (3) trace regressions to a specific rule or batch.

Core ideas (high-level):
1) Minimal provenance fields to capture per-label: annotator_id | label_type | rule_id | rule_version | confidence | adjudicated_by | adjudication_note | timestamp. Keep names short, stable.
2) Distinguish microclass assignment source into 4 buckets: human_manual, human_adjudicated, auto_rule, auto_model_suggest.
3) For auto_rule, require rule_id and rule_sha or PR link. For model_suggest, capture model_version and suggestion_confidence.
4) If label is converted from a macro-class later split into microclasses by heuristics, store original_macro and split_reason.

Lightweight provenance schema (proposal):
- label: <string> (the microclass)
- source: one of [human_manual, human_adjudicated, auto_rule, auto_model_suggest]
- actor: <annotator id or system id>
- confidence: <0-1 float as string>
- rule_id: <optional string> (e.g., rules/email-format-v2)
- rule_ref: <optional url or PR id>
- model_version: <optional>
- adjudicator: <optional>
- note: <optional free text>
- timestamp: ISO date
(We will store these as string fields in CSV/Parquet; keep them short to reduce schema churn.)

Heuristics for when to use microclass vs fallback macro: (working rules)
- If annotator confidence < 0.6 OR source=auto_model_suggest with confidence<0.5 => annotate with macro + provenance note: "micro-fallback:low_confidence" and tag the microclass that was suggested in note.
- If disagreement >=2 among 3 annotators on micro label => use macro with adjudication flag and queue for discussion (store the 3 votes in provenance blob).
- If tokenization ambiguity (e.g., hyphenation, merged tokens) undermines micro resolution => fallback to macro with note "tokenization-uncertain" and sample for tokenizer-fix experiment.

Example labeled row (CSV-friendly format):
- text: "Book a flight to St. Louis on 5/5"
- label: "intent.book_flight.domestic"
- source: "human_manual"
- actor: "aj_ramanathan_v1"
- confidence: "0.95"
- rule_id: ""
- rule_ref: ""
- model_version: ""
- adjudicator: ""
- note: ""
- timestamp: "2024-11-02T13:22:00Z"

Ambiguous examples we need canonical handling for (notes):
1) Short-form names: "Call Dr. Lee" -> is "Dr. Lee" an ENTITY.person or ENTITY.medical_pro? For microclass, we should only pick "medical_specialist" when surrounding tokens indicate appointment context OR matching medical-title token. Otherwise microclass should be "person_title" (macro: person).
2) Multi-intent single utterance: "Find vegan spots and book a table" -> prefer split into two micro-intents when downstream supports multi-intent; otherwise label macro intent "multi/booking_search" and set micro suggestions in note.
3) Time expressions: "next Fri" vs "Fri" (relative vs absolute) -> microclass normalize: prefer "time.relative.weekday" only when anchored to a reference time in metadata; otherwise keep macro "time.expression".

Adjudication protocol (quick):
- Triage path: low-confidence votes or >1 conflict -> send to 2nd-pass adjudicator (senior labeler).
- Adjudicator fills adjudication fields (adjudicator id, timestamp, rationale).
- If second-pass still disagrees, escalate to labeling lead with flagged examples and propose either: change spec, add rule, or accept soft labels (probabilistic).

Mini-experiment notes (results):
- Sampled 200 examples where microclass was auto_suggest by model v3 with suggestion_conf > 0.7: human acceptance rate ~68% (n=136). Most rejections were edge phrase variants (abbrev & punctuation).
- Small rule patch "rules/title-disambiguation-v1" fixed ~22/40 of those rejections when applied pre-suggestion (PR: labeling-rules/pull/88).

Operational concerns / UX for labeling tool (todo list):
- Show source badge (human/manual, auto-rule, model-suggest) in UI with color and hover to show rule_ref.
- Make a one-click fallback: "use macro instead" that sets provenance fields automatically.
- Exporter should be able to filter (exclude auto_rule) for high-quality eval sets.
- Backfill pipeline: when rule changes, we must be able to re-run derivation and mark rows with previous_rule_version -> keep an audit trail.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we enforce confidence thresholds globally, or per-microclass? (Some microclasses inherently harder; per-class thresholds might reduce unnecessary falls to macro.)
- How to represent multi-label micro assignments succinctly in CSV? Comma-separated labels vs repeated rows? (Prefer repeated rows with label provenance per-row for traceability.)
- For storage: do we keep a small JSON blob column for provenance or split fields? Pros/cons: blob = flexible but harder to query; split fields = schema churn. Leaning split fields with a single "prov_blob" optional text for extras.

Immediate next steps (personal todo):
- Draft a short Confluence page with the proposed minimal schema and examples (start from linked_artifacts).
- Add unit tests for exporter that ensure provenance fields survive dedupe + merge.
- Run a 1k-sample audit to compute per-microclass agreement and propose per-class thresholds.

Quick notes / stream-of-consciousness (raw):
- we should add a tiny "rule_conflict" tag if a rule sets a microclass but a model_suggest disagrees >0.3 -> useful signal for rule rot.
- when an auto_rule fires, always append rule_ref with PR id so rollback is practical.
- prefer short stable ids for annotators (e.g., aj_ramanathan_v1) not full emails.
- capture tool version in provenance; sometimes UI tweaks change interpretation.

References and links (handy):
- Slack thread: #labeling-microclasses (see pinned messages)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/labeling-rules/pull/88 (title: "title-disambiguation: detect honorifics")
- JIRA: LABEL-912 (task: microclass provenance schema)

End of scratchbook. Will refine and move to shared Confluence when stable enough.

TODOs appended: 
- [ ] Turn schema into JSON Schema + small converter for CSV exports.
- [ ] Add a dev ticket to capture rule_ref automatically on rule deploy.
- [ ] Schedule 30m sync with Jonah + Mariana to pick adjudication SLAs.
